title: ROUND: money to two decimals
prompt: In B6, total the three costs, add 8% markup, and round the result to 2 decimals.

require.message: The total is summed before it is rounded: wrap the range in SUM.

hints.syntax: =ROUND(SUM(B2:B4)*1.08,2) — the arithmetic first, then how many decimals.
hints.func-round: ROUND takes two arguments: the number, and the number of decimals. Without it the answer runs on for four decimals.
hints.func-sum: Add the three line items with SUM rather than typing the total.
hints.require-ref: The formula has to read the cost cells so next month's invoice changes the answer.
hints.value: Check the order of operations: the whole total gets the markup, and ROUND applies to the result. 4120.74 × 1.08 = 4450.3992, which rounds to 4450.40.
hints.error: #VALUE! means ROUND was handed text instead of a number: make sure SUM(B2:B4)*1.08 is what sits inside ROUND, and that the range picked up no header cell.

docs.explain: The three line items are 1500.24, 1120.5 and 1500, which total 4120.74. Adding an 8% markup means multiplying by 1.08: 4120.74 × 1.08 = 4450.3992. ROUND with 2 decimals turns that into 4450.4 — note that the trailing zero is a formatting question, the stored value is 4450.4 either way. The important part is that ROUND changes the value, while formatting the cell only changes what you see: a total that looks like 4450.40 after formatting is still 4450.3992 in the sum of the next column, and that is where a penny appears in an invoice. A negative num_digits rounds to tens or hundreds, so ROUND(4450.3992,-2) gives 4500.

errors.text: One of the two arguments is missing or the decimal count is text, for example "2" in quotes from a copy-paste.
ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN and ROUND are different functions; a misspelling gives #NAME?.
Rounding each line item before adding gives a different total from rounding the sum, and invoices are disputed over exactly that.

docs.atWork: Quotes, invoices and price lists all live or die on two decimal places. The professional habit is to round the final figure once, not every intermediate step.
docs.outcome: Round money after applying the markup, not before.
